chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Fuzayl ibn Khaysam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'An army of ten thousand would not be defeated due to scarcity (of numbers)'.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the relationship between army size and victory?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys the Prophet’s assurance that a force of ten thousand will not be defeated due to scarcity of numbers, emphasizing that divine support (tawfiq) and spiritual quality often outweigh mere numerical superiority. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is frequently interpreted to highlight the principle that a small, faithful group backed by God can overcome a larger, disorganized enemy, a theme central to the Battle of Badr. It serves as a theological foundation for the concept of 'qillat al-‘adad' (fewness) not being a weakness when accompanied by divine favor.
